name: From Sequins to Sloths: Northern Brazil for the Chronically Curious
lede: When you are seeking that spark of life, you chase it. Carnaval in Salvador with 2.5 million people, a desert that fills with water every year, and six days on the Rio Negro with pink dolphins and one sloth with somewher

name: I Drove Across Denmark to Watch a Million Birds Go to Bed
lede: A last-minute trip to the German border for Sort Sol, the marshland murmuration that only does the famous part when something tries to eat it. Plus the falcon that never showed, and the correct way to cross the Fyn bridg

name: La Paz, whale sharks, and a sea lion who chose chaos
lede: Wider than your sense of scale, moving with an ease that is almost funny once the initial shock wears off. Then the sea lions, who chose chaos.

name: Patagonia, measured in Camp Italianos
lede: Some people do vision boards. We did blisters. An accelerated W Trek over Christmas, a rainbow nobody deserved, and a New Year in the golden light at Estancia Bonanza.

name: The annual retreat, or what happens when you put a Mangalitsa fillet and a switchback road in a blender
lede: Montenegro's roads are about to get a quiet word from Nepal, Austria and Croatia. Narrow, one-way as a suggestion, with semi-trucks reversing down mountains.

name: Ghana asked us to wear all white. We complied. Eventually.
lede: Denmark had just thrown the coldest winter in 16 years at us, the map had a gap, and we had a few days. Then we landed in a country where everyone was wearing white except us.

name: Fourteen days, twelve countries, one EV, and a gal who cannot be historically trusted to charge her own phone
lede: Copenhagen to Kosovo and back in an EV, with one Samoyed operating in an advisory capacity and a back seat that ended up looking like a small artisan jam factory in transit.

name: Whiskey on 10,000-Year-Old Ice and Chasing the Impossible: The Antarctica Marathon
lede: The honeymoon that became a four-year cancellation saga, and then the coldest, strangest, most beautiful race I have ever run. Four attempts, one pandemic, and an apartment marathon I recommend to nobody.

name: My Unique Experience at Horseshoe Bend
lede: A five-hour drive from Phoenix that almost didn't happen, a crowd of strangers all saying wow at the same rim, and a long climb down to the Colorado River to kayak.

name: Spain: A Wedding and an Adventure
lede: A friend's wedding outside Madrid, free tapas with every drink, a Keinemusik night at La Caja Mágica, then a villa in Ibiza and a ferry to Formentera.

name: Salty dips in two seas and a pastry-filled road trip across Scandinavia
lede: As one does, my friends arrived, so I took them to a Danish bog. Three countries, one opinionated Samoyed, a lot of pastries, and a trip bookended by the North Sea and the Baltic.

name: Four Cubs and the Smoke
lede: Four countries, five out of the Big 5, one race that ended in a medical vocabulary lesson she did not ask for, and a mama lion with four cubs tumbling off a log that rearranged her entire understanding of joy.

name: Twelve Days Above the Treeline
lede: Ten strangers, 92.9 miles, 18,519 feet, and a turboprop cockpit recording blaring danger-danger terrain pull up before they had even started walking.

name: Six Down, One to Go
lede: Eighteen months after foot surgery, she ran 42 kilometers through a river gorge that looked CGI'd. Continent six of seven, pain-free for the first time in years.

name: Two Countries, Four Espressos a Day
lede: Four women. 260 kilometers across Portugal and Spain. Ten days. Enough Compeed to tile a small cathedral and one Portuguese swear word that refused to stop following obrigada.

name: The Beautiful Beast
lede: Nine hikers. Twenty-eight crew. Eight days on the Lemosho Route, one mountain that does not care about your fitness tracker, and a summit sunrise that made every frozen finger worth it. Team Sexy Awesome assembled.

name: The Place That Chose Me
lede: You do not pick where you are from. It picks you somewhere between the first rainy hike and the first sunrise you can never photograph, and after that you are just carrying it around in every country.

name: The Country That Sounds Like Swallowing
lede: Three years in Copenhagen taught her that hygge is real, the loneliness is louder than expected, and the best pine cone you will ever eat costs four hundred dollars. She arrived for a two-year contract. She left with a h

name: The Glistening Desert I Never Planned to Call Home
lede: A visa that was processing became a forty-day residency in 120-degree heat. She arrived displaced, sweat-drenched, and alone. She left with tan lines, a desk full of dates, and the resilience nobody warns you about.

name: Welcome to Sampa
lede: She arrived expecting a layover city and left two years later with a Samoyed, a Morton's neuroma the surgeon was genuinely giddy about, and the ability to be in the place where she actually was.
